Subject: Recap + next tests: networking & air-gap feasibility

Thanks again for the time today — good call. Recap + proposed next steps below so we can align with your infra/NOC team.

Recap (short):
- Primary ask: confirm feasibility of Private/VPC (control plane in your VPC) and fully air-gapped on-prem option for model inference.
- Constraints: no outbound control-plane traffic preferred for some environments; strict KMS/HSM requirements called out by procurement.
- Key stakeholders: Sarah (Security/Infra), Michael (SRE/Platform), NOC for firewall changes.

Proposed next tests (we suggest a 2-3 day run):
1) Network connectivity check — allowlist IPs and small control-plane handshake (no model traffic). We provide a short test agent and IP list.
2) Control-plane reachability options — validate Private control plane in your VPC vs our hosted control plane with tunneled provisioning.
3) Air-gap feasibility checklist — what minimal outbound is required for on-prem installer vs fully offline install.

Can you confirm: preferred test window (we penciled Thu 20 Aug 10:00-12:00 PT), NOC contact, and whether procurement needs an updated SOW or NDA before we proceed?

I've attached a networking matrix and a short air-gap checklist to start. Marissa (solutions) and Vivek (infra eng) are copied and will own the test design and runbook.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30 min pre-test call with NOC if helpful.

—

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear summary. A few notes from our side:

- NOC contact: Alicia Park (alicia.park@acmehealth.com) — she'll own firewall rules and scheduling.
- Preferred window: Thu 20 Aug 10:00-12:00 PT works for us.
- Control plane: for our regulated workloads we prefer the control plane to run inside our VPC (private control plane). If that isn't possible for some features, we need to know exactly which control-plane calls require outbound access and whether those can be proxied via an internal NAT to a redwood endpoint.
- Air-gapped: procurement wants clarity on whether Redwood supports a fully offline installer (no outbound) vs an initial provisioning step that requires temporary outbound connectivity. Our legal/KMS team also needs details on HSM integration (we use AWS CloudHSM).

If you can call out which of the following are required vs optional that would help:
- Ports and IPs to allow for control-plane and health checks
- Any outbound TLS endpoints for telemetry or licensing
- Where keys live (customer-managed KMS/HSM) and how key material is accessed

Procurement also asked for an updated SOW and a copy of your standard SOC2 evidence package (redacted). If you can send an NDA/DocuSign link for procurement to countersign that would speed things up.

We'll loop Alicia into the pre-test call; can you send a calendar invite for Thu?

—
Sarah Green

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next tests: networking & air-gap feasibility

Thanks Sarah — quick technical notes and proposed test plan from our side. I'm Marissa (solutions eng); Vivek will help run the infra tests.

High-level options (what we can offer):
A) Private control plane (recommended):
   - We deploy a small control-plane component into a customer subnet (we provide an AMI/container image you run in your VPC).
   - Required outbound: none for normal inference traffic — all model/data stays in your VPC. Control-plane telemetry is optional and can be disabled.
   - Required networking: our control-plane needs access to internal registry (optional) and to your KMS endpoint for signing (we support AWS KMS/CloudHSM).
   - Ports/IPs: for the control-plane component we need egress to AWS KMS endpoints and optional egress to Redwood update endpoint (if you choose auto-updates). If you opt-out of auto-updates, we can do signed offline bundles.

B) Fully air-gapped on-prem package (offline install):
   - We provide an air-gap installer and a signed bundle. By design this requires zero outbound shipping after install.
   - Caveat: initial provisioning (optional) can be done via secure USB transfer or via a one-time, short-lived outbound call to redeem licenses if you want live telemetry. We can avoid that if you prefer manual signing and offline key injection.

Proposed test plan for Thu 20 Aug (10:00-12:00 PT):
1) NOC firewall test (10:00-10:30) — Alicia opens allowlist for the test-control IPs we provide (we'll send a CIDR list).
2) Control-plane handshake (10:30-11:15) — deploy a temporary control-plane container in a test subnet and verify provisioning + KMS sign/verify flows. We'll run a small handshake and then tear down.
3) Air-gap checklist review (11:15-12:00) — walk the offline installer flow and confirm what artifacts you'd need for a fully offline install.

Deliverables we'll bring to the call: networking matrix (attached), air-gap checklist (attached), minimal IP list (will send separately), and a one-page SOW addendum for this eval. We'll also include a redacted SOC2 summary for procurement.

A couple of specifics you asked about:
- Ports: 443 for TLS to KMS endpoints (customer-managed). We don't require any additional outbound ports for a private control plane.
- Telemetry/licensing: optional and can be disabled. If enabled, it can be proxied through a customer-managed egress.
- HSM: we support customer-managed CloudHSM via standard PKCS#11 interfaces; we do not extract key material.

I'll circulate a calendar invite for Thu and include Alicia (NOC). If you want a quick 15m sync with your procurement team beforehand to review the SOW language, let us know a time.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
